subject: dentistry
intro: Dentistry leads to the oral health team — general dentists and specialists restoring mouths, hygienists preventing disease, and the assistants and laboratory technicians who make clinical dentistry work.

roles.title: Dentists, General
roles.what: Examine, diagnose and treat diseases, injuries and malformations of teeth and gums, treating the nerve and pulp tissues that affect oral health and fitting dental appliances or providing preventive care.
roles.where: Caries and restorative dentistry, periodontology, endodontics and oral medicine — the clinical spine of the course — are exactly the diagnostic and restorative work of general practice.

roles.title: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons
roles.what: Perform surgery and related procedures on the hard and soft tissues of the oral and maxillofacial regions, treating diseases, injuries or defects and sometimes operating to improve function or appearance.
roles.where: Trauma management from the endodontics and pulp unit, craniofacial anatomy, pain and anxiety control, and the systemic-disease links in oral medicine underpin the surgical pathway.

roles.title: Prosthodontists
roles.what: Diagnose, treat, rehabilitate, design and fit prostheses that maintain oral function, health and appearance for patients with clinical conditions of the teeth, oral and maxillofacial tissues or the jaw.
roles.where: The prosthodontics and occlusion unit — fixed and removable prostheses, occlusal principles, implant dentistry — plus the dental biomaterials strand are this specialty's core curriculum.

roles.title: Dental Hygienists
roles.what: Administer oral hygiene care to patients, assess oral hygiene problems and needs, maintain health records and advise on oral health maintenance and disease prevention, with advanced care such as fluoride treatment.
roles.where: Periodontology — the tissues, disease classification, therapy and maintenance — and the screening and prevention strands of health promotion are the hygienist's clinical bread and butter.

roles.title: Dental Assistants
roles.what: Perform limited clinical duties under a dentist's direction — preparing and sterilising equipment, preparing patients for treatment, assisting the dentist during procedures and instructing patients in oral healthcare.
roles.where: Infection control in the operatory and pain and anxiety control from the patient management unit, plus handling dental biomaterials, are the exact chairside skills this role practises.

roles.title: Dental Laboratory Technicians
roles.what: Construct and repair full or partial dentures and dental appliances — the crowns, bridges and prostheses that dentists prescribe for their patients.
roles.where: Dental biomaterials — amalgam, composite, ceramics and impression materials — and the prosthodontics unit's occlusal principles give you the materials and design knowledge the laboratory bench demands.
